color-contrast (light) — date-picker/cal.note: 2.23:1, measured 2026-08-14. A design call, not a patch, and NOT the WCAG exemption the route baseline claims for it: out-of-month days are enabled `<button>`s (`disabled=false`, `aria-disabled=false`) reachable with the arrow keys, so 1.4.3 applies to them. The colour is right — `--wr-calendar-muted` is `#5f6c7d`, which clears AA on white at 4.63:1 — and `opacity: 0.55` is what drops it to 2.23. Raising the opacity does not fix it either: at 0.75 the composite is #87919e (3.2:1), and reaching 4.5 needs essentially the full-strength muted colour, which is the same tone as an in-month day. So the de-emphasis and the ratio cannot both be had by tuning this one number — it wants a different signal (weight, a dot, a divider) or non-actionable out-of-month days.

color-contrast (dark) — date-picker/cale.note: 3.11:1, the same element and the same design call as the light entry — #5a6374 on #0b1120. Dark starts closer because the muted role lightens, and the 0.55 opacity is still what puts it under.

color-contrast (light) — calendar/today-.note: The same out-of-month cells as the date-picker entry, reached through `wr-calendar` directly rather than through a picker's popup — 2.23:1, 17 nodes across the page's three calendars. One design call, two states that paint it.

color-contrast (dark) — calendar/today-a.note: 3.11:1, the dark half of the entry above.

color-contrast (light) — slider/thumb-fo.note: 2.43:1 on the DISABLED slider in that demo, and genuinely exempt: WCAG 1.4.3 does not apply to an inactive control. axe cannot tell, because `disabled` sits on the `<wr-slider>` host rather than on the label it is measuring — the same blind spot the route baseline records for `<wr-btn disabled>` labels. Only the light theme lands under 4.5; dark clears it.

target-size (light) — window/open.note: 14×14px where WCAG 2.5.8 wants 24, found the first time anything measured an OPEN window — `check:contrast` walks pages at rest, where the chrome does not exist. A design call in the same family as the carousel dots, and the reason it is not a quiet patch: these are traffic-light buttons, and 24px ones are a different title bar. There IS a fix that keeps the look — give the button a 24px box and paint the 14px dot with a `::before` — but it changes the chrome's spacing, so it is the maintainer's call rather than a gate's.

target-size (dark) — window/open.note: The same three buttons at the same 14×14px — the chrome is not themed.

target-size (light) — carousel/dot-activ.note: 8×8px dots (20×8 for the active one) where WCAG 2.5.8 wants 24, and centres 14px apart, so the undersized-target spacing exception does not rescue them either. Already recorded in `contrast-baseline.json` as a design call — it appears here too because hovering a dot is a state, and the rule fires on the element either way. Fix them in one place and both entries go.

target-size (dark) — carousel/dot-active.note: The same dots at the same size — not themed.
